topic: federal carbon tax and enumerated powers
text: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Calder County's legal review concluded that a federal carbon levy administered through 14 separate agencies could not be audited by any single one of them. No agency held both the emissions data and the receipts, so no agency could say what the tax had actually cost or collected.

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. In Mourne Ridge the levy raised the average household heating bill by 312 dollars in its first winter. The promised rebate arrived the following August, eight months later, and 22 percent of eligible households never filed the form required to claim it.

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Every carbon levy Calder County examined arrived with exemptions for its largest emitters, negotiated before passage. The four largest facilities in Mourne Ridge paid an effective rate of 11 percent of the headline figure, while households paid the full amount.

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Mourne Ridge's own municipal levy, set locally and repealable by local ballot, cut emissions 9 percent in three years. The county argues the mechanism was not the price but the fact that the people paying it could end it, which a federal tax removes.

topic: federal carbon tax good faith of revenue neutrality
text: FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DATA. Of the six jurisdictions Calder County surveyed that promised revenue neutrality, four had diverted receipts to general funds within five years. Revenue neutrality was a feature of the first budget and of no subsequent one.
